new_candidates.body:
## Summary

In `behavior-1k-assets` 3.9.0, the collision meshes of `objects/bookcase/vgzdul` sit about **+1.476 m along the model's local x axis** away from its visual mesh (same size, unscaled model units). In every scene that places this model, the physical bookcase is therefore an invisible box next to the visible one:

- the robot is stopped on empty-looking floor next to the bookcase, and
- the robot can drive into the visible bookcase.

The floor traversability maps (`layout/floor_trav_0.png`, `floor_trav_no_door_0.png`, `floor_trav_open_door_0.png`) follow the collision geometry, so they show a blocked strip on empty floor and free space where the bookcase is drawn.

## Versions

- `behavior-1k-assets` 3.9.0 (the scene JSONs record `behavior-1k-assets 3.9.0rc9`, `omnigibson 3.8.0`). The same blocked strips are in the 3.7.2rc1 maps.
- OmniGibson from `StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K` main @ `6559858`.

## 1. The model file

Extents in the model frame (mesh points × prim-to-root transform), from `objects/bookcase/vgzdul/usd/vgzdul.encrypted.usd`:

| part | x | y | z |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_link/visuals` (1 mesh) | [-0.178, +0.179] | [-0.967, +0.957] | [-0.937, +0.882] |
| `base_link/collisions` (8 meshes) | **[+1.288, +1.666]** | [-0.967, +0.973] | [-0.907, +0.924] |

For comparison, `bookcase/njwsoa`, `bookcase/owvfik` and `bed/mpgavt` have collision and visual extents that coincide within a few cm.

## 2. The traversability maps

For each of the 17 placements of `vgzdul` (10 scenes), fraction of the (80 %-shrunk, rotated) footprint that the map marks as blocked by objects (`floor_trav_no_obj_0` free and `floor_trav_no_door_0` blocked), at the pose stored in `<scene>_best.json` and at that pose shifted by 1.476 m × scale_x along the object's local +x:

| scene | object | yaw | scale_x | blocked at stored pose | blocked at shifted pose |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Beechwood_0_garden | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 180.0 | 0.833 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Beechwood_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 180.0 | 0.833 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Beechwood_1_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | -89.5 | 1.354 | 0.00 | 0.84 |
| Benevolence_1_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 0.3 | 0.333 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Ihlen_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 0.0 | 1.038 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Merom_1_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 179.4 | 0.333 | 0.65 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_garden | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 0.0 | 0.916 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_garden | bookcase_vgzdul_1 | 180.0 | 1.029 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_garden | bookcase_vgzdul_2 | 89.3 | 0.784 | 0.98 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_garden | bookcase_vgzdul_3 | 0.0 | 1.327 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | -89.5 | 1.077 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_1 | -178.7 | 0.916 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_2 | 0.0 | 1.029 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_3 | -89.5 | 0.784 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_0_int | bookcase_vgzdul_4 | 180.0 | 1.327 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_1_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 180.0 | 1.090 | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Pomaria_2_int | bookcase_vgzdul_0 | 90.0 | 0.748 | 0.00 | 1.00 |

The shifted footprint is blocked in all 17 placements; the stored footprint is free in 13 of them (where it is blocked, other objects stand there). Other objects in the same maps line up with their stored poses (e.g. in Pomaria_2_int `bed_mpgavt_0` 1.00, `bottom_cabinet_rntwkg_0` 0.98, `bookcase_owvfik_0` 0.94).

## 3. In the simulator

In Pomaria_2_int (`bookcase_vgzdul_0`, yaw 90°, scale_x 0.748, so the colliders sit 1.10 m north of the visible bookcase), we drove the robot (Tiago, OmniGibson from BEHAVIOR-1K main) straight south with `move_forward` × 4 (0.25 m per step) from three starts. Step outcomes as reported by the simulator:

| start (x, y), facing south | steps 1–4 | stopped at y | `collision_path` of the blocking step |
|---|---|---:|---|
| (-2.5, -1.05): towards the empty floor where the colliders are | succeeded, partial, blocked, blocked | -1.504 | `/World/scene_0/bookcase_vgzdul_0/base_link/collisions/vgzdul__base_link__collision__3` |
| (-2.5, -2.30): towards the visible bookcase (its front face is at y = -2.75) | succeeded, succeeded, partial, blocked | -2.889 | `/World/scene_0/walls_ewvyod_0/base_link/collisions/ewvyod__base_link__collision__4` |
| (-1.5, -1.95): towards `bottom_cabinet_rntwkg_0` (control) | succeeded, partial, blocked, blocked | -2.369 | `/World/scene_0/bottom_cabinet_rntwkg_0/link_1/collisions/rntwkg__link_1__collision__3` |

So the robot is stopped by the bookcase's colliders on empty floor, and drives into the visible bookcase until the wall behind it stops it (in the follow camera after the second run, the robot stands inside the bookcase). The control run stops at the cabinet's front face as expected.

## 4. Other models

We compared visual and collision extents for all 3,707 models used by the 51 scenes. Among floor-standing objects only `bookcase/vgzdul` is displaced like this; `gate/vqjuvg` (Beechwood_0_garden) has a collision body about 1 m thicker than its visual mesh. The remaining mismatches are walls, ceilings, signs, paintings and switches.

## Reproduce

`repro.py` below only reads BEHAVIOR files: `python repro.py <path to behavior-1k-assets>`. It prints the table in section 1 and the table in section 2.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproduce: bookcase/vgzdul collision meshes are offset from the visual mesh (behavior-1k-assets 3.9.0).

Usage:  python repro.py <path to behavior-1k-assets>      (needs numpy, pillow, usd-core, cryptography;
        the decryption key is read from <assets>/../omnigibson.key, as OmniGibson does)

Part 1 reads the model USD and prints the extent of the visual mesh and of the collision meshes in the model frame.
Part 2 reads every scene's <scene>_best.json and floor_trav_no_door_0.png / floor_trav_no_obj_0.png and, for each
vgzdul placement, prints the fraction of its footprint that the map marks as blocked by objects at the pose stored
in the scene file, and at the pose shifted by 1.476 m * scale_x along the object's local +x axis.
"""
import glob, json, math, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

A = Path(sys.argv[1])

# ---- part 1: model file
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
from pxr import Usd, UsdGeom
enc = A / "objects/bookcase/vgzdul/usd/vgzdul.encrypted.usd"
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    dec = Path(td) / "vgzdul.usd"
    dec.write_bytes(Fernet((A.parent / "omnigibson.key").read_bytes()).decrypt(enc.read_bytes()))
    stage = Usd.Stage.Open(str(dec))
    prefix = stage.GetDefaultPrim().GetPath().pathString + "/"
    xc = UsdGeom.XformCache(Usd.TimeCode.Default())
    ext = {}
    for prim in stage.Traverse():
        p = prim.GetPath().pathString
        if not prim.IsA(UsdGeom.Mesh) or not p.startswith(prefix):
            continue
        part = p[len(prefix):].split("/")
        if len(part) < 3 or part[0] != "base_link" or part[1] not in ("visuals", "collisions"):
            continue
        pts = np.asarray(UsdGeom.Mesh(prim).GetPointsAttr().Get(), np.float64)
        w = (np.c_[pts, np.ones(len(pts))] @ np.asarray(xc.GetLocalToWorldTransform(prim)))[:, :3]
        lo, hi = ext.get(part[1], (np.full(3, np.inf), -np.full(3, np.inf)))
        ext[part[1]] = (np.minimum(lo, w.min(0)), np.maximum(hi, w.max(0)))
for k, (lo, hi) in sorted(ext.items()):
    print(f"base_link/{k:10s} x [{lo[0]:+.3f}, {hi[0]:+.3f}]  y [{lo[1]:+.3f}, {hi[1]:+.3f}]  z [{lo[2]:+.3f}, {hi[2]:+.3f}]")
(vlo, vhi), (clo, chi) = ext["visuals"], ext["collisions"]
shift = ((clo + chi) / 2 - (vlo + vhi) / 2)[0]
print(f"collision centre - visual centre along local x: {shift:+.3f} m (unscaled)")

# ---- part 2: traversability maps vs scene poses
size = np.array(json.load(open(A / "objects/bookcase/vgzdul/misc/metadata.json"))["bbox_size"])


def frac(mask, cx, cy, hx, hy, yaw):
    ys, xs = np.mgrid[-1:1:21j, -1:1:21j]
    lx, ly = xs.ravel() * hx, ys.ravel() * hy
    wx = cx + lx * math.cos(yaw) - ly * math.sin(yaw)
    wy = cy + lx * math.sin(yaw) + ly * math.cos(yaw)
    n = mask.shape[0]   # OmniGibson map_base.world_to_map: row = y/res + n/2, col = x/res + n/2, res = 0.01
    r = np.clip((wy / 0.01 + n / 2).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
    c = np.clip((wx / 0.01 + n / 2).astype(int), 0, n - 1)
    return float(mask[r, c].mean())


print(f"\n{'scene':20s} {'object':20s} {'yaw':>6s} {'scale_x':>7s}  blocked@pose  blocked@pose+{shift:.3f}*scale_x")
for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(A / "scenes/*/json/*_best.json"))):
    scene = Path(f).parts[-3]
    d = json.load(open(f))
    reg, info = d["state"]["registry"]["object_registry"], d["objects_info"]["init_info"]
    names = [k for k, v in info.items() if v["args"].get("model") == "vgzdul"]
    if not names:
        continue
    lay = A / "scenes" / scene / "layout"
    trav = np.array(Image.open(lay / "floor_trav_no_door_0.png")) >= 255
    noobj = np.array(Image.open(lay / "floor_trav_no_obj_0.png")) >= 255
    objmask = noobj & ~trav               # blocked by objects only (walls excluded)
    for name in names:
        x, y, _ = reg[name]["root_link"]["pos"]
        qx, qy, qz, qw = reg[name]["root_link"]["ori"]
        yaw = math.atan2(2 * (qw * qz + qx * qy), 1 - 2 * (qy * qy + qz * qz))
        s = info[name]["args"]["scale"]
        hx, hy = 0.8 * size[0] * s[0] / 2, 0.8 * size[1] * s[1] / 2
        k = shift * s[0]
        print(f"{scene:20s} {name:20s} {math.degrees(yaw):6.1f} {s[0]:7.3f}  {frac(objmask, x, y, hx, hy, yaw):12.2f}  "
              f"{frac(objmask, x + k * math.cos(yaw), y + k * math.sin(yaw), hx, hy, yaw):12.2f}")
```
</details>

## Suggested fix

Move the 8 collision meshes of `bookcase/vgzdul` by -1.476 m along local x (or re-export them from the visual mesh), then regenerate the traversability maps of the 10 scenes above.
new_candidates.title: `bookcase/vgzdul`: collision meshes are offset ~1.48 m from the visual mesh (invisible obstacle in 10 scenes, also in the traversability maps)

new_candidates.body:
## Summary

`asset_pipeline/b1k_pipeline/usd_conversion/make_maps.py` marks a 1 cm cell traversable only if a box from `Z_END = -0.1` to `Z_START = 2.0` m hits nothing but floors. Many door headers (the wall collider above a doorway) have their bottom at exactly 2.00 m, so the box touches them and the whole doorway is drawn as wall — also in `floor_trav_no_door_0.png`, where the doorway is open and a robot drives through it in the simulator.

## Versions

- `behavior-1k-assets` 3.9.0; `StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K` main @ `6559858` (same `make_maps.py`).

## What we measured

- In the 26 scenes we use there are 200 doorways in wall colliders. At 99 of them the doorway centre is blocked in `floor_trav_no_door_0.png`, and a robot-sized footprint can cross only 124 of the 200. Most of the closed ones have a header whose collider bottom is at exactly 2.00 m (61 doorways). In 6 scenes `floor_trav_no_door_0.png` is pixel-identical to `floor_trav_0.png` (Benevolence_1_int, Benevolence_2_int, Ihlen_0_int, Merom_0_int, Merom_1_int, Rs_int).
- In the simulator (OmniGibson from BEHAVIOR-1K main, doors removed from the scene), a Tiago drives through all 6 map-closed doorways we tried (`move_forward`, every step `succeeded`).
- Re-running `generate_maps_for_current_scene` unchanged except `Z_START = 1.87` (our robot's highest point plus 5 cm) on the same scenes: 98 of the 99 closed doorway centres open, and the robot footprint can cross 183 of the 200 doorways (of the 13 left, 9 lead outside the building where there is no floor). The room segmentation maps do not change. Elsewhere the maps differ only where something sits between 1.87 and 2.0 m (e.g. tree canopies in the garden scenes) plus a few-cm sliver at a handful of objects.

## Suggestion

Make the query height a parameter (or derive it from the robot), or at least stop just below 2.0 m so that headers placed at exactly 2.0 m are not hit. A one-line repro: in any of the 6 scenes above, `og.sim.psqi.overlap_box` with half height `(2.0 + 0.1) / 2` centred at `z = 0.95` in a doorway reports the wall; the same query with the top at 1.87 m reports only the floor (that is the height we redrew with; we did not test values between 1.87 and 2.0 m).
new_candidates.title: Traversability maps close doorways whose header sits at 2.0 m (`make_maps.py` queries up to exactly `Z_START = 2.0`)

new_candidates.body:
### Description

Rarely, the app segfaults inside `libomni.syntheticdata.plugin.so` while `SyntheticData._post_process_graph_tick` evaluates its graph. It runs headless, with cameras and annotators. I've seen it three times:
- at the first renders after the timeline starts (1 in 11 starts);
- at a render after reloading a stage (1 in 70+ runs);
- mid-run in Isaac Lab 3.0.0rc1, 32 envs with two cameras, on a normal step (1 in 4 runs).

From the minidumps: all three crash at the same instruction (plugin offset `0x137f0d`, `mov 0x10(%r13),%rcx`), in a loop over 32-byte records. The array's pointer and count don't agree: twice the pointer was NULL with a count of 3, and once it was valid with a count of about 250 million. That suggests the tick reads a stale or freed object. The last command before each crash was `CreateAttrCommand` on `state:_sdp_intergraph_downstream_node_handles_`.

I can't trigger it on demand. 240 runs aimed at the first two cases didn't crash.

### Isaac Sim version

6.1.0 (`VERSION`: 6.1.0-rc.26+release.49347.2d230af4.gl), Kit 110.3.0, omni.syntheticdata 0.6.17

### Operating System (OS)

Ubuntu 24.04

### GPU Name

RTX 4090

### GPU Driver and CUDA versions

Driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2 (the first crash was on driver 595.91.07)
new_candidates.title: Segfault in omni.syntheticdata during the post-process graph tick (Isaac Sim 6.1.0)
